title: FeatureSpec
description: Structured spec of a paper's design feature, emitted by the distiller node. Downstream integration agents implement against this document, so it must be complete enough to implement without the paper.

source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
source.citation: Toru Koizumi, Toshiki Maekawa, Masanari Mizuno, Maru Kuroki, Tomoaki Tsumura, and Ryota Shioya. 2025. RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables. In Proceedings of the 6th Championship Branch Prediction (CBP 2025), in conjunction with ISCA 2025, June 21, 2025, Tokyo, Japan, pp. 1-6.

summary: The sR component extends the statistical corrector (SC) of a TAGE-SC-L branch predictor to exploit global correlations between recently produced architectural register values and branch outcomes. Rather than tracking register dependencies directly per branch, sR compresses values from all completed instructions into 12-bit digests and tracks their validity in a 65-entry Tomasulo-like table with an instruction-age decay counter (invalidated after 256 decoded instructions). The registers are distributed across 8 banks. For each bank, 3 small usefulness tables (UT) index usefulness weights by PC to select the most useful valid register in the bank. The chosen register digest and PC then index 3 prediction weight tables (WT). When a bank's selected register has positive usefulness, its WT sum is scaled by 2.5x (and suppressed to 0x otherwise); the 8 bank outputs are summed to form sR, which feeds into the overall SC summation (LSUM). This mechanism is especially effective immediately following pipeline squashes when execution backend completions outpace fetch restart.

state.name: sR_WT
state.organization: 8 banks; each bank contains 3 direct-mapped sub-tables: WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), WT2 (128 entries); 7,168 entries total across all banks
state.indexing: WT0: hash(PC, digest, 0) % 512 (9-bit index); WT1: hash(PC, digest, 1) % 256 (8-bit index); WT2: hash(PC, digest, 2) % 128 (7-bit index)

state.name: sR_UT
state.organization: 8 banks; each bank contains 3 direct-mapped sub-tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) of 8 entries each. Bank 0 tracks 9 logical registers (R0, R8, ..., R64); Banks 1 through 7 each track 8 logical registers (R_i where i % 8 == bank_id)
state.entry_format: Vector of 6-bit signed saturating counters [-32, 31] per tracked register in the bank: Bank 0 entries contain 9 x 6-bit weights (54 bits/entry); Banks 1-7 entries contain 8 x 6-bit weights (48 bits/entry)
state.indexing: UT0: hash(PC, 0) % 8 (3 bits); UT1: hash(PC, 1) % 8 (3 bits); UT2: hash(PC, 2) % 8 (3 bits), using independent PC bit-skewing functions

state.name: reg_tracking_table
state.organization: Direct-mapped table with 65 entries corresponding to logical registers R0 through R64
state.entry_format: valid: 1 bit; payload: 14 bits (holds 14-bit in-flight ROB index when valid=0, or 12-bit register digest zero-extended when valid=1); decay_ctr: 8-bit unsigned counter
state.indexing: Directly indexed by logical register index (0 to 64)

algorithms.name: generate_digest
algorithms.trigger: Execution/writeback time when a functional unit produces an architectural register value
algorithms.pseudocode:
function generate_digest(val: uint64, reg_type: enum { INT, FP16, FP32, FP64, FLAG }) -> uint12:
    switch reg_type:
        case INT:
            trailing_zeros = count_trailing_zeros(val)
            trailing_ones = count_trailing_ones(val)
            trailing_count = (val & 1) ? trailing_ones : trailing_zeros
            trailing_field = min(trailing_count, 63) & 0x3F

            leading_zeros = count_leading_zeros(val)
            leading_ones = count_leading_ones(val)
            leading_count = ((val >> 63) & 1) ? leading_ones : leading_zeros
            leading_field = min(leading_count, 63) & 0x3F

            lsb_field = val & 0x3F
            return trailing_field ^ (leading_field << 3) ^ (lsb_field << 6)

        case FP16:
            // Val[15:13] placed at digest[5:3]
            return ((val >> 13) & 0x7) << 3

        case FP32:
            // Val[31:26] placed at digest[8:3]
            return ((val >> 26) & 0x3F) << 3

        case FP64:
            // Val[63:55] placed at digest[11:3]
            return ((val >> 55) & 0x1FF) << 3

        case FLAG:
            // 4-bit condition flags replicated 3 times into digest[11:0]
            flags = val & 0xF
            return flags | (flags << 4) | (flags << 8)

    return 0
algorithms.notes: Digest generation compresses 64-bit data into a 12-bit signature. For integer values, XOR overlapping folds trailing identical bits [5:0], leading identical bits [8:3], and LSBs [11:6]. For floating point values, the sign and highest exponent bits are aligned starting at digest bit 3 with bits [2:0] set to 0. For flags, 4 bits replicate across all 12 bits.

algorithms.name: dispatch_rename
algorithms.trigger: Decode / Rename stage when an instruction writing a destination logical register enters the pipeline
algorithms.notes: Clearing the valid bit prevents in-flight, uncommitted values from being read as digests, while the ROB tag allows matching upon completion.

algorithms.name: writeback_complete
algorithms.trigger: Writeback / Execution completion stage when an instruction produces a result value
algorithms.notes: Once execution completes, the digest becomes available immediately to front-end branch lookups, even before instruction retirement.

algorithms.name: decay_tick
algorithms.trigger: Decode stage, invoked once for each instruction decoded
algorithms.notes: Enforces freshness. Stale register digests degrade accuracy and are evicted after 256 instructions have been decoded.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.trigger: Lookup time (fetch / branch prediction stage) for conditional branches
algorithms.notes: Computes sR to be added into LSUM. The usefulness tables act as an arbiter to pick the most correlated register within each bank. If usefulness is non-positive or no register is valid, that bank contributes 0.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.trigger: Commit time (or branch execution resolution) when the branch predictor trains
algorithms.notes: Only registers that were valid at prediction time are eligible for training. If multiple registers in a bank were available, one is randomly sampled for update to require only a single write port per table.

algorithms.name: squash_recovery
algorithms.notes: Entries awaiting values from flushed instructions have their invalid in-flight tags cleared. Valid digests from instructions that finished execution before the squash remain valid and accelerate post-recovery predictions.

host_interfaces.need: Logical destination register ID and ROB index at instruction decode/dispatch
host_interfaces.description: Host front-end must provide the destination architectural register index (0..64) and allocated ROB tag for any instruction writing a register.
host_interfaces.fallback: If ROB tags are unavailable, in-flight instruction sequence numbers modulo 16384 (14 bits) can be substituted.

host_interfaces.need: Produced register value and register type at functional unit execution writeback
host_interfaces.description: Host execution units must forward the 64-bit output value, register type (INT, FP, FLAG), and associated destination register ID/ROB tag upon operation completion.
host_interfaces.fallback: If FP or FLAG classifications are unavailable, treat all 64-bit values as INT and apply the INT digest folding.

host_interfaces.description: Host decoder signals each decoded instruction to advance the 8-bit decay counters in the register tracking table.
host_interfaces.fallback: Tick decay counters once per fetch cycle or every N cycles based on nominal machine IPC.

host_interfaces.need: Pipeline flush notification with squashed ROB index range
host_interfaces.description: Host must indicate which in-flight instructions are squashed during a branch misprediction redirect to clear invalid pending entries.
host_interfaces.fallback: Conservatively clear the valid bits of all registers where valid == 0 upon any pipeline flush.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: WT (Prediction Weight Tables): 6 bits * (512 + 256 + 128 entries) * 8 banks = 43,008 bits; UT (Usefulness Weight Tables): 6 bits * 65 registers * (8 + 8 + 8 entries) = 9,360 bits; Auxiliary Data (Tracking Table): 65 registers * (1-bit valid + 14-bit payload + 8-bit decay_ctr) = 1,495 bits. Grand Total = 53,863 bits (6,732.875 bytes ~ 6.58 KiB).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Requires 8 parallel 8-to-1 / 9-to-1 comparator trees to select maximum usefulness in each bank; 12-bit digest generators (leading/trailing zero count logic and XOR trees) at execution units; 2.5x fixed-point multiplier (x * 2 + x / 2) on the bank weight sums; 8-operand adder tree for sR.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: To fit within iso-storage (e.g. 192 KiB total), sR can be funded by: (1) shrinking the large Bimodal table by ~43,000 bits (e.g. reducing Bimodal entries from 128K to ~93K or 64K entries), or (2) removing 1 or 2 banks from the 25 High-bank tagged TAGE tables (each bank is 34,816 bits).

parameters.name: num_banks
parameters.storage_impact: Directly scales the number of WT banks and the register partitioning width in UT

parameters.name: weight_width
parameters.storage_impact: Directly scales entry size of WT and UT tables

parameters.name: decay_instruction_limit
parameters.storage_impact: num_logical_registers * ceil(log2(decay_instruction_limit)) bits in tracking table

parameters.name: num_logical_registers
parameters.storage_impact: Scales UT vector width and reg_tracking_table entry count

unit_tests.name: int_digest_generation_check
unit_tests.given: 64-bit integer value 0x0000000000000008 (leading zeros = 60, trailing zeros = 3, LSB[5:0] = 8)

unit_tests.name: fp64_digest_generation_check
unit_tests.expect: Digest slice Val[63:55] shifted to bits [11:3] produces digest = 0x80 << 3 = 0x400 (bits [2:0] = 0)

unit_tests.name: flag_digest_generation_check
unit_tests.given: Flag value with condition code nibble 0b1011 (0xB)

unit_tests.name: digest_decay_invalidation
unit_tests.given: Register R4 receives valid digest at cycle 0. 256 instructions are decoded without new writes to R4.
unit_tests.expect: At the 256th decoded instruction, R4 decay_ctr saturates/exceeds 255 and valid bit transitions from 1 to 0

unit_tests.name: bank_usefulness_selection_and_gating
unit_tests.given: Bank 0 has two valid registers: R0 with UT sum = +5, and R8 with UT sum = -2. WT sum for R0's digest is +10.
unit_tests.expect: R0 is selected as largest usefulness (+5 > -2). Because usefulness > 0, bank 0 output is scaled: 10 * 2.5 = 25. If R0's usefulness were <= 0, bank 0 output would be gated to 0.

unit_tests.name: post_squash_retention
unit_tests.given: Instruction producing R1 completes execution and sets valid=1. Branch mispredicts and squashes pipeline.
unit_tests.expect: R1 remains valid=1 in reg_tracking_table across the squash redirect, allowing immediate post-flush branch predictions to correlate on R1's digest.

open_questions: INT count encoding ambiguity: Figure 6 specifies 6-bit widths for leading and trailing one/zero counts (which can take values 0..64 in a 64-bit register). Assumed behavior is saturating counts at 63.
INT one vs zero count selection: The text mentions 'the count of leading zeros (or ones)'. Assumed behavior: counts leading bits matching the sign bit (MSB) and trailing bits matching the LSB.

Training register selection: When multiple registers in a bank were available at prediction time, the paper states one is selected randomly. Assumed pseudo-random selection or round-robin as a deterministic fallback.

FP classification logic: The mechanism for classifying whether a 64-bit register currently contains FP16, FP32, or FP64 is unspecified in hardware; assumed to rely on host ISA execution unit tags or operand type tracking.
Gating condition for x0 vs x2.5: Figure 5(c) shows 'x0 or x2.5'. Assumed to be driven by (max_usefulness > 0) of the selected register in that bank.

[/parameters/5] What is the optimal weight bit-width across target area and accuracy budgets?

[/algorithms/0/pseudocode] The paper states that the most significant bits are inspected to classify the format, but does not specify the exact bit patterns or classification algorithm used to distinguish FP16, FP32, and FP64.
[/parameters/9] The paper does not state whether sR weight table training is triggered at branch execution/resolution or at architectural commit.
[/parameters/10] The paper does not specify the exact training update condition for sR weight tables among matching branch direction, correcting TAGE, or TAGE mispredictions only.
[/parameters/11] The paper explicitly defers recovery of the Tomasulo-like table following pipeline flushes to future work, leaving the post-squash recovery policy unspecified.
[/parameters/12] The paper does not specify whether leading and trailing identical bit counts saturate at 63 or wrap modulo 64 when all 64 bits are identical.

[/algorithms/6] Section 5 explicitly states that recovering the Tomasulo-like table is future work; the paper does not specify how flushed in-flight entries are identified or whether a flushed ROB bitmask is used. Additionally, the 'if(...)' syntax flagged in the deterministic findings represents a built-in language conditional rather than an undefined helper function. How should in-flight entries be handled upon squash?

[/algorithms/5/pseudocode] The paper states that UT tracks prediction usefulness 'as with the SC's existing components', but does not specify the exact mathematical condition for updating UT weights—specifically whether the update delta is determined solely by the sampled register's WT prediction matching the outcome (pred_sign == taken), or whether it depends on whether the register contribution would have corrected an overall misprediction or agreed with the final SC prediction.
[/algorithms/0/pseudocode] Does integer digest generation choose between counting zeros versus ones based on the edge bit (LSB/MSB), count only zeros, or count whichever run is non-zero?
[/algorithms/0/pseudocode] When a 64-bit integer contains 64 identical bits, does the 6-bit count field saturate at 63 or wrap modulo 64?
[/algorithms/1/pseudocode] Does dispatch_rename reset decay_ctr, or is decay_ctr initialized to 0 when the instruction completes and the valid digest is written?

[/host_interfaces] Does the host interface provide an explicit squashed ROB index range or mask to clear in-flight tracking entries on a pipeline flush, or does the predictor flash-invalidate invalid entries or perform no recovery?
[/parameters/9] Does SC training update occur at branch commit or at execution resolution?
[/parameters/10] Under what condition are sR weight tables updated during training?
[/parameters/11] Which recovery policy should be applied to reg_tracking_table on a pipeline flush?
[/parameters/13] How are FP operand widths (FP16, FP32, FP64) distinguished from 64-bit register values when generating digests?
[/parameters/14] What mechanism clears in-flight speculative entries upon a pipeline squash redirect?
[/algorithms/6] How should squashed in-flight register entries be invalidated in the Tomasulo-like tracking table given that Section 5 defers table recovery to future work?
[/algorithms/4] The paper specifies the table dimensions and indexing inputs (PC and 12-bit digest) but omits the exact bitwise hash functions for hash_pc and hash_wt.

[/algorithms/5] The paper specifies training uses register values available at prediction time, but does not state whether the 12-bit digest is checkpointed in the branch state or re-read from the tracking table at commit.
